title: FIVE.
paragraphs:
You thought it was just a number.
But it keeps showing up… right when you’re at your worst.

Because we read the Bible for stories—
but God writes in patterns.

And five keeps appearing…
right where failure should have ended everything.
Right where shame should have had the final word.

Not to a perfect version of you—
but to the real one.
The one who knows what it’s like to fall… again.

The one who smiles in public but replays guilt in private.
The one who promised, “This is the last time…”

Like heaven is keeping count—
and you’ve already gone too far?
Because Scripture doesn’t hide broken people.
Then it floods them with something they didn’t earn.
David picked up five smooth stones.

“Then he took his staff in his hand, chose for himself five smooth stones from the brook… and he drew near to the Philistine.”
— 1 Samuel 17:40
Standing before a giant that mocked him, defied God, and should have crushed him.
And yet—only one stone was used.

Because even before the victory—
God was already declaring something deeper:
“This will not be about your strength.”

The law of God—His holy standard—
is written in the first five books of the Bible.

“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.”
— Romans 3:23

God is holy.
You are not.

The law exposes it.
Your conscience confirms it.
So where does five—grace—fit into this?
Right where you think it’s over.

Because the same Bible that gives the law…
introduces Jesus.

“For the law was given through Moses; grace and truth came through Jesus Christ.”
— John 1:17

Law reveals the problem.
Grace reveals the Savior.
And then this detonates everything you thought you knew about God:

“But where sin increased, grace increased all the more.”
— Romans 5:20
You thought your sin disqualified you.
God says it became the stage where His grace would be displayed.

Your secret sin?
He saw it.

Your hidden addiction?
He knows it.
That thing you’re ashamed to even name?
This is where most people run.
But this is exactly where God steps in.
Because grace is not God ignoring your sin.
Grace is God dealing with it fully—through Jesus Christ.
Not just by mistake… but by nature.
And sin separates you from God.

“For the wages of sin is death…”
— Romans 6:23
Because the verse doesn’t end there.

“…but the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.”
— Romans 6:23

Jesus lived the life you couldn’t live.
Perfect. Sinless. Obedient.
Then He died the death you should have died.
On the cross, your sin was not ignored—it was punished.

“God made Him who knew no sin to be sin for us, so that in Him we might become the righteousness of God.”
— 2 Corinthians 5:21
So what do you do with this?
You don’t clean yourself up first.
You don’t wait until you feel worthy.

“Repent, then, and turn to God, so that your sins may be wiped out…”
— Acts 3:19

Because the same God who placed five stones in David’s hand…
is placing grace in front of you.
It’s not about defeating a giant.
You are not too far gone.
And if something inside you is stirring—
